chapter: Midwest bands: Hardy Brothers, Helvey and Buffalo
title: Leaving Helvey's band for Luke Stewart's telegram offer in Buffalo
summary: After a battle of bands in Louisville against Purdue's Pirates, he accepted Luke Stewart's wire for a 35-week trumpet opening, learning he had to go it alone sometimes.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: But this was before I got there. This was when Luke was there. So I got back and it was nice to seem him and talk to him, and we stayed around there for awhile and then we left. We stayed down there about, oh, two months, working a steady job, and then we left and went out to tour some more, through Pennsylvania and Ohio and all around. And then we went back home to play a battle of music with a band in Louisville called Purdue's Pirates, and they had the two bands playing, and Helver's Troubadors, in a battle of music, you know. And so we got into that. And while playing that, I get a telegram out there from Luke Stewart the guitar playing, and saying, 'Have opening for trumpet. Let me know if you'd like to take it.' 35 weeks. So, I wired him back and told him yes, you know. I hated --
So by now you're ready to go out all by yourself.

I hated to leave this band, you know. I hated to leave all the guys, you know, I'd been with. But I found out then, I says, no, you just can't go and have a buddy all the time, you know. You've got to go by yourself sometimes.
So I went on in Buffalo.
How old were you by then? Would you say nineteen?
